profile.reading: This is KIO Networks second Spanish data center, in Paterna, in the Valencia metropolitan area, developed at an investment of more than 50 million euros and originally expected to open around November 2024 after about 18 months of construction. The facility offers 1,000 square meters of Tier IV certified IT room space with 2.4 megawatts of total power capacity, including 1 megawatt dedicated to servers, across 80 server racks each holding roughly 2,500 servers. KIO built the site around sustainability focused cooling: a closed loop system that uses water only once, to fill the circuit at startup, after which no further water is needed for the life of the facility, paired with liquefied CO2 as the primary refrigerant, which the operator describes as making it the first data center in Spain to use 100 percent ecological refrigerants under European F-GAS regulations, further supported by a geothermal system of 71 wells drilled 150 meters deep with more than 2,000 meters of piping circulating water in a closed loop to help manage summer temperatures. The project was expected to create about 70 direct jobs. KIO Networks Espana, the joint entity behind both this facility and the operators original Murcia site, became wholly owned by Spanish retail conglomerate El Corte Ingles after it completed a buyout of the remaining stake from Mexican parent KIO Networks, registered with Spains Commercial Registry by November 27, 2024. KIO Networks, the Mexican parent brand behind the original 50 percent stake in this Spanish joint venture, was founded in 2002 and is headquartered in Mexico City, describing itself as a leading provider of carrier neutral digital infrastructure and data center services across Mexico and other Latin American markets, with facilities including two in Queretaro, Mexico rated around 18 to 19 megawatts each.
profile.research_note: Researched fresh 2026-09-04 via Valencia Plaza local press coverage of the Paterna facility construction and Murcia Plaza coverage of the El Corte Ingles ownership transaction.

reading.body:
Spain added 2.4 megawatts of data center capacity near Valencia with a facility designed around water conservation and ecological cooling, signaling how European operators are building new compute infrastructure within environmental constraints.

KIO Networks' Paterna facility demonstrates the infrastructure tradeoffs now shaping data center development. The site uses 1,000 square meters to deliver 2.4 megawatts, with cooling via geothermal wells and CO2 refrigerants rather than water-intensive systems. This reflects European environmental regulation and water scarcity pressures that do not equally constrain facilities in other regions. The 2.4 megawatts supports roughly 2,500 servers across 80 racks, meaning power availability remains the limiting factor on compute density even in newly built centers.

The facility's investment scale and ownership trajectory reveal how data center development is concentrating in larger corporate portfolios. A 50 million euro investment for 2.4 megawatts of capacity aligns with European construction costs, and El Corte Ingles's acquisition of the Spanish operations from the Mexican parent shows retail and logistics conglomerates viewing digital infrastructure as a strategic asset. This does not indicate whether Spanish power grids can supply additional facilities at this scale, only that capital is available to build where regulatory approval exists.

The data covers facility specifications and ownership but does not address grid connection timelines, power purchase agreements, or whether Valencia's regional grid expansion matches new demand from this site and others planned nearby.
